resources.string: For your security, Firebase asks for a recent sign in for this. Sign out, sign in again, then try again.
On: signing in asks for a code of your authenticator app
Off: turn it on to also ask for a code of an authenticator app
Signing in to TermiNow asks for a code of %1$s after the password or Google.
Signing in will only need the password or Google again. You can turn 2FA on again later.
1. Add this key to an authenticator app, like Google Authenticator, Microsoft Authenticator or 2FAS:
No authenticator app opened it. Install one, or copy the key and add it by hand.
2. Enter the %d-digit code that the app shows:
Keep the authenticator app: without it you can not sign in. Your hosts, keys and files on this phone never depend on it.
Enter the code of the authenticator app
Enter the code that your authenticator app shows for TermiNow.
Enter the code that %1$s shows for TermiNow.
2FA is not turned on for TermiNow yet on the server. It will work once it is.
The password you sign in to TermiNow with
The two new passwords are not the same
Your other devices are signed out and sign in with the new password. The password of the vault does not change.
You sign in with Google, so there is no TermiNow password to change.
The devices signed in to this account, and signing them out
A device you sign out is signed out the next time TermiNow opens on it. Sign out everywhere ends every session at once, this device included.
Sign out %1$s? Its hosts, keys and files stay on it.
Every device is signed out of this account, this one too. Hosts, keys and files stay on each device.
This device was signed out of your account from another device. Your hosts, keys and files are still here.
The devices of the account are not on the server yet. Try again later.
Off: keys and identities stay on this phone
On: end-to-end encrypted in the Personal vault
On: waits for the Personal vault to sync

The private keys of the Keychain and the identities are added to your Personal vault and go to your other phones. They are encrypted on this phone with the vault key before they are uploaded: the server can not read them.\n\nBiometric keys and security keys never leave this device. A key that another phone has with the same name is never replaced.
The Personal vault is only on this phone now: syncing it is set up next.
Keys and identities are taken out of the Personal vault at the next sync, for all your phones. They stay on every phone that has them.

Termius can not export its data, so TermiNow moves it in two steps.

1. Hosts: pick an SSH config (like ~/.ssh/config of a computer) or a CSV with the columns of Termius (Groups, Label, Tags, Hostname, Protocol, Port, Username, Password, Key).

2. Keys: in Termius, open each key in Keychain and copy its private key, then come back here: it is filled in. Hosts that name the key get it.

Passwords and keys are encrypted on this phone. Delete the CSV afterwards.
Next, paste these keys from Termius: %1$s.
In Termius, open a key in Keychain and copy its private key, then come back here. If Termius does not show it, copy the key file from the computer it came from.
No private key is copied yet
The hosts and their keys are in TermiNow.
These keys are still missing, so their hosts have no key yet: %1$s. Paste them later with More keys, or in Keychain.
